top_choice_rationale: P002 rests on one sharp, complete idea: the magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the clock-transition light shift so many atoms are interrogated at once, realised by Katori and Ye and reproduced by independent clocks at about 10^-18. The interpretation is settled, the credit is the cleanest on the slate, and the consequences (relativistic geodesy, constant-drift limits, redefinition of the second) are concrete. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is real but concerns different tools; the incomplete credit to the NIST, PTB and RIKEN groups is acknowledged. P001 follows as the best theory-plus-experiment split, though its mechanism is unsettled and it is only eight years old; P004 follows as a mature, well-confirmed achievement that sits closer to the 2012 prize.
recusal_note: Possible conflict: I work in the same atomic physics, quantum optics and precision laser spectroscopy area as P002 and P004, and have a research stay in John Hall's laboratory (Hall shared the 2005 prize for the comb and laser-based precision spectroscopy, on which P002 builds); no documented direct tie to Katori, Ye, Cirac, Zoller or Blatt.
